tooltip.title: The "How" of Diagnosis
tooltip.markdown: An overview of the essential tools and tests used to arrive at a definitive diagnosis for alopecia.

tooltip.title: Trichoscopy (Scalp Dermoscopy)
tooltip.markdown: Non-invasive visualization of the scalp and hair shafts. Considered an essential part of the modern hair loss consultation.

tooltip.title: Trichoscopy of Androgenetic Alopecia
tooltip.markdown:
-   **Hallmark Sign:** Hair shaft diameter diversity >20% (anisotrichosis).
-   **Other Signs:** Increased single-hair units, perifollicular pigmentation, empty follicles (yellow dots).

tooltip.title: Trichoscopy of Alopecia Areata
tooltip.markdown:
-   **Active Disease:** Exclamation mark hairs, black dots (cadaverized hairs), broken hairs.
-   **Chronic Disease:** Yellow dots (sebaceous gland openings).
-   **Regrowth:** Short vellus hairs, pigtail (circle) hairs.

tooltip.title: Trichoscopy of LPP/FFA
tooltip.markdown:
-   **Hallmark Sign:** Perifollicular scaling (tubular casts).
-   **Other Signs:** Perifollicular erythema, loss of follicular openings, "lonely hair" sign in FFA.

tooltip.title: Trichoscopy of Discoid Lupus
tooltip.markdown:
-   **Key Signs:** Thick arborizing (branching) blood vessels, follicular keratotic plugs.
-   **Other Signs:** Follicular red dots, speckled blue-gray dots (pigment incontinence).

tooltip.title: Trichoscopy of Neutrophilic Alopecias
tooltip.markdown:
-   **FD:** Hair tufts (>5 hairs per unit), follicular pustules, yellowish crusts.
-   **DC:** AA-like empty follicles in early stages; later shows cutaneous clefts with emerging hairs ("3D" appearance).

tooltip.title: Scalp Biopsy
tooltip.markdown: The gold standard for definitively diagnosing scarring alopecias and confirming inflammatory non-scarring alopecias.

tooltip.title: Indications for Biopsy
tooltip.markdown:
-   When the diagnosis is in doubt.
-   To definitively differentiate scarring from non-scarring alopecia.
-   To assess for prognosis or document permanent hair loss.

tooltip.title: Biopsy Technique
tooltip.markdown:
-   **Standard:** A 4-mm punch biopsy is preferred to ensure an adequate number of follicles.
-   **Depth:** Must extend into the subcutaneous fat to include the hair bulbs.
-   **Sectioning:** Horizontal (transverse) sectioning is most valuable for quantifying follicles and evaluating architecture.

tooltip.title: Biopsy Site Selection
tooltip.markdown:
-   **Scarring Alopecia:** Biopsy the **active edge**, identified by clinical inflammation (redness, scale) or trichoscopic features. Avoid the bald, end-stage center.
-   **Non-Scarring Alopecia:** Biopsy the area of most severe thinning or the active border of a patch.

tooltip.title: Laboratory Evaluation
tooltip.markdown: Labs are guided by the clinical history and differential diagnosis. There is no standard universal panel.

tooltip.title: Labs for Diffuse Hair Loss
tooltip.markdown: Investigations are selected from the history and examination, for example CBC and ferritin when iron deficiency is plausible and TSH when thyroid disease is suspected. Correct documented deficiencies. A ferritin target of 40–70 ng/mL for hair regrowth and routine vitamin-D testing for every patient are not established by the sources supplied here.

tooltip.title: Labs for FPHL with Hyperandrogenism
tooltip.markdown: Indicated if female patient presents with acne, hirsutism, or irregular menses.
